source1: John F. Hansman, 'Elymais', Encyclopaedia Iranica (1998, updated 2013) - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elymais
notes: Hansman: c. 221 CE Ardashir, rebel from Fars, defeated last king Orodes and took Elymais's major city; this conquest 'marked the end of Elymais as a political state'. Britannica concurs (extinction by Ardashir I). Database end 215 slightly early.

successor: Egypt - Mamluk Sultanate II (same Turkish/Qalawunid sultanate)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Egypt: The Mamluk and Ottoman periods (1250-1800)' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Egypt/The-Mamluk-and-Ottoman-periods-1250-1800
source2: Amalia Levanoni, 'The Mamluks in Egypt and Syria: the Turkish Mamluk sultanate (1250-1382) and the Circassian Mamluk sultanate (1382-1517)', New Cambridge History of Islam vol. 2, Cambridge UP 2010 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/new-cambridge-history-of-islam/mamluks-in-egypt-and-syria-the-turkish-mamluk-sultanate-64878412501382-and-the-circassian-mamluk-sultanate-78492313821517/570A843BCC929EACFC485F822BF6354F
notes: No break in 1348: Qalawunid sultans ruled until 1382 inside the same Mamluk state, which lasted to 1517. 1348 (plague year) is a period boundary. Q4: rapid depositions of al-Nasir Muhammad's sons after 1341.

successor: Aztec Empire (Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Mexico: The rise of the Aztecs' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Mexico/The-rise-of-the-Aztecs
source2: Frances F. Berdan, 'El tributo a la Triple Alianza', Arqueologia Mexicana 124 (2013), pp. 49-55 - https://arqueologiamexicana.mx/mexico-antiguo/el-tributo-la-triple-alianza-0
notes: Tepanec hegemony of Azcapotzalco overthrown 1428 by its own tributaries (Mexica paid it tribute) allied with Texcoco and Tlacopan; Huexotzinco aid never controlled the core. Q4: Tepanec-Texcoco war 1418, Maxtla's 1426 usurpation. DB end 1426.

successor: Kingdom of Saba (continued at Marib until Himyarite annexation c. 275 CE)
source1: Jeremie Schiettecatte, 'Saba'', Thematic Dictionary of Ancient Arabia (2024) - https://ancientarabia.huma-num.fr/dictionary/definition/saba
source2: Alessandra Avanzini, 'Qataban', Thematic Dictionary of Ancient Arabia - https://ancientarabia.huma-num.fr/dictionary/definition/qataban
notes: From the 5th c. BCE Saba lost hegemony (mukarrib title replaced by king) as Qataban and Hadramawt rose, but the kingdom persisted at Marib until Himyar absorbed it c. 270-275 CE. Qataban never held Marib. Chronology debated.

successor: Timurid Empire (Timur, Barlas amir of the Chaghatay ulus)
source1: Peter Jackson, 'Chaghatayid dynasty i. History', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/chaghatayid-dynasty/i-history/
source2: Bertold Spuler, 'Central Asia v. In the Mongol and Timurid periods', Encyclopaedia Iranica (1990) - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/central-asia-v
notes: From the 1340s tribal amirs ruled Transoxiana with puppet khans; fragmentation after 1358; Tughluq Temur's 1360 reunification was intra-Chaghatayid. Insider amir Timur killed rival Husayn, ruled by 1370 with nominal Ogedeid khans. DB 1402 = last nominal khan.

source1: J. Stephen Athens, Timothy M. Rieth, Thomas S. Dye, 'A Paleoenvironmental and Archaeological Model-Based Age Estimate for the Colonization of Hawai'i', American Antiquity 79(1), 2014 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-antiquity/article/paleoenvironmental-and-archaeological-modelbased-age-estimate-for-the-colonization-of-hawail/A831E7C6BED967D22E33C905FE1CD3FA
source2: Tom Dye, 'Population Trends in Hawai'i Before 1778', Hawaiian Journal of History 28 (1994) - http://www.pelagicos.net/BIOL3010/readings/Dye_1994.pdf
notes: Initial colonization phase (settlement c. 940-1130 CE), no recorded central authority. Dye shows continuous population growth from founding into the 1150-1450 Growth Phase, so continuity into Hawaii II. Some chronologies place settlement later (1200s).

successor: Egypt - Late Old Kingdom (6th Dynasty, Teti)
source2: Tara Prakash, 'Egypt in the Old Kingdom (ca. 2649-2130 B.C.)', Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, Metropolitan Museum of Art (2019) - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/oking/hd_oking.htm
notes: 2350 BCE marks the 5th-to-6th Dynasty change (Unas to Teti, his son-in-law) within the same Memphite Old Kingdom state; decline of central power came later in Dynasty 6. Britannica dates Dynasty 5 end c. 2306 BCE.

successor: Kingdom of Aksum (Aksumite-installed king, then Abraha)
source2: Iwona Gajda, 'Himyar', Thematic Dictionary of Ancient Arabia (2023) - https://ancientarabia.huma-num.fr/dictionary/definition/himyar
notes: Aksumite army crushed Himyar c. 525 (Gajda: c. 522), killed king Yusuf and installed a client king; Aksumite general Abraha then ruled; Sasanians took Yemen c. 570. Q4: Yusuf seized power c. 522 by fighting the Aksumite-backed order.

source1: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site' - https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/198/
source2: Larry V. Benson, Timothy R. Pauketat, Edward R. Cook, 'Cahokia's Boom and Bust in the Context of Climate Change', American Antiquity 74(3), 2009 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/american-antiquity/article/cahokias-boom-and-bust-in-the-context-of-climate-change/450C4880F8F28C35181AFBF94A075B38
notes: Emergent Mississippian (Terminal Late Woodland) village phase in the American Bottom, no recorded central authority. Occupation continuous; pre-Mississippian villages persisted until Lohmann-phase reorganization c. 1050, so 900 is a phase division. Indirect evidence only.

source1: Pierre Briant, 'Alexander the Great', Encyclopaedia Iranica (1985) - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/alexander-the-great
notes: 333-332 BCE Alexander took Phoenicia: Sidon, Byblos, Arados surrendered, keeping tributary monarchies under a Macedonian satrap; Tyre resisted seven months and was destroyed. Q4: Sidonian revolt against Persia 351-345 BCE (Schmitt, Iranica 'Artaxerxes III').
